# Patches against @medplum/ccda 5.2.15

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/tree/v5.2.15/packages/ccda (Apache-2.0, see LICENSE).

| # | File | Change | Why | Upstream |
|---|------|--------|-----|----------|
| 0 | all `*.ts` | mechanical: strip-only TypeScript: relative imports get `.ts`; `index.ts` no longer re-exports `./fhir-to-ccda/convert` | Node runs .ts directly; `fhir-to-ccda/` is not vendored | none (GA only) |
| 1 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `oids.ts` | section entries routed by any of the section's templateIds (`getTemplateIds`), not `templateId[0]`; Medications entries-optional and V2 roots routed; `OID_PROBLEMS_SECTION_V2_ENTRIES_REQUIRED` loses its stray space. Test `test/section-template-order.test.ts` | Epic lists the entries-optional root first: every Epic document threw (or, ignoring unsupported sections, lost its medications); replaces GA's `promote()` pre-pass | existing issue medplum#10671 (proposes this fix; no PR yet); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/1-section-template-order.md` |
| 2 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | an observation with no templateId (and a goal with no statusCode) converts: `processObservation` uses `getTemplateIds(observation)` (a goal matched by any of its templates), `mapGoalLifecycleStatus` reads `statusCode?.` Test `test/observation-without-template.test.ts` | `observation.templateId[0]` threw a TypeError and refused the whole document | new issue (none open); may fold into the #10671 PR, same cause; draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/2-observation-without-template.md` |
| 3 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `types.ts` | external PR medplum#11242 applied unchanged (head c1e81639): narrative references (`#id`) resolve to the section narrative text in codes; text `ED` observation values become `valueString`. Test `test/narrative-reference.test.ts` (ported to vitest) | note, instruction and referral entries (rows 5-6) carry their text only by reference; ED values were dropped (Task 7's ED half lands here) | existing PR medplum#11242 (fixes #11202, #10659); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/3-narrative-references.md` |
| 4 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | care team organizer: every member act (`component.act[]`) and every performer of each act becomes a `CareTeam.participant` (`processCareTeamMembers`). Test `test/care-team-members.test.ts` | only `component.act[0]` and `act.performer[0]` were read; other members were silently lost | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/4-care-team-members.md` |
| 5 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `oids.ts` | a Note Activity (`22.4.202`) in any section, and every act in the Notes (`22.2.65`), Instructions (`22.2.45`, V2) and IHE History of Present Illness (`1.3.6.1.4.1.19376.1.5.3.1.3.4`, new `OID_HISTORY_OF_PRESENT_ILLNESS_SECTION`) sections, becomes a `DocumentReference`: text/plain attachment (the act text or the narrative it references, via row 3), type = act code, category = section code, context.period from effectiveTime, author, source ids. Test `test/note-sections.test.ts` | these entries were skipped (Notes: "not yet implemented"; the others unsupported); notes are what GA's `notes_search` reads | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/5-note-sections.md`; needs medplum#11242 |
| 6 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | acts in the IHE Reason for Referral section (and V2) become a `ServiceRequest`: status and intent from statusCode/moodCode, category SNOMED 3457005 "Patient referral", code, occurrence, requester (author), performers, narrative text as `note`, source ids. Test `test/referral-section.test.ts` | referrals were skipped ("not yet implemented") | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/6-referral-section.md`; needs medplum#11242 for the text |
| 7 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `types.ts`, `xml.ts` | Payers section (and V2): each Policy Activity of a Coverage Activity becomes a `Coverage`: identifier (policy id, then covered party member id), status `active` (C-CDA has none), type (policy code), beneficiary, subscriberId (policy holder id), relationship and period (covered party), payor (payer performer org id and name; data-absent `unknown` when none), order (sequenceNumber). `processAct` may return several resources. `act.participant` parsed as an array; `CcdaParticipant.time`. Test `test/payers-section.test.ts` | payers were skipped ("not yet implemented"); the Microsoft path made Coverage. Guarantor and the policy holder's own name/address have no Coverage field: GA names them in notImported | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/7-payers-coverage.md` |
| 8 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | a Plan of Treatment act's CarePlan `description` is the act's own text or the narrative it references (via row 3), with the narrative-reference extension. Test `test/care-plan-text.test.ts` | `nodeToString(act.text)` was empty for a `<reference>`, so the plan text lived only on the (never shared) Composition | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/8-care-plan-text.md`; needs medplum#11242 |
| 9 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | a problem, health concern or allergy concern act becomes one `Condition` / `AllergyIntolerance` per SUBJ observation (`getSubjectObservations`), not only `entryRelationship.find(SUBJ).observation[0]`. Each record's identifiers are its own observation ids first, then (first record only) the act ids (`mapConcernIdentifiers`); `AllergyIntolerance` gains `identifier` (it had none). Test `test/concern-observations.test.ts` | a concern may track several problems or allergies; all but the first were silently lost. Observation id first: it is the per-record id (the act id is shared), as the Microsoft path keyed them. Known limits: a later observation (index > 0) with no id has no identifier, so GA keys it by content hash (a changed value makes a new record); a first observation with no id is keyed by the act id | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/9-concern-observations.md`. medplum#11308 (allergy category, Task 8) touches the same allergy body: its hunk's context (`id: this.mapId(act.id)`) no longer matches, so apply its change inside `processAllergyIntoleranceObservation` by hand |
| 10 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | an Encounter Diagnosis act (`22.4.80`, V2 `22.4.80.2`) inside an encounter, under any entryRelationship typeCode (Epic: SUBJ; IG: REFR), becomes one `Condition` per SUBJ problem observation (row 9's builder, `processConditionAct(act, ENCOUNTER_DIAGNOSIS)`): category `encounter-diagnosis`, `encounter` → its Encounter. Test `test/encounter-diagnoses.test.ts` | visit diagnoses were silently dropped (only RSON observations were read): the spike lost 106 of 138 Conditions. Link Condition → Encounter only (child to parent), so the Encounter is unchanged and no reference cycle forms | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/10-encounter-diagnoses.md` |
| 11 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `xml.ts` | `<title>` is a parser stop node (`stopNodes: ['*.title']`): its raw inner XML, in document order (attributes still under `@_`). The document title, each Composition `section.title` and a note's `attachment.title` (row 5) are plain text (`nodeToPlainText`, exported: tags removed, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed). Test `test/title-markup.test.ts` | a title with markup (`Patient <content>Instructions</content>`) parsed to an object, so the record was invalid FHIR and GA refused the note (a loss); the parsed object also lost the word order. GA's `sectionName` uses the same function | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/11-title-markup.md` |
| 12 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `systems.ts` | fork commit jacekprzybyl/medplum@6f245b1 (fix for medplum#10847) applied by hand onto row 1's routing: in Plan of Treatment a substanceAdministration's `moodCode` sets `MedicationRequest.intent` (`PLANNED_MEDICATION_MOOD_MAPPER`: PRP → proposal, INT/PRMS → plan, RQO → order; missing → order); Medications section stays `order`; a single `effectiveTime/@value` becomes `dispenseRequest.validityPeriod.start`. Test `test/planned-medication.test.ts` (ported to vitest, ONC-sample case dropped: its testdata file is not vendored) | a planned or proposed medication read as an authorized order, the same shape as a current one; a planned time was dropped (`validityPeriod: {}`) | existing issue medplum#10847, fix on the author's fork (no PR yet); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/12-planned-medication-mood.md` |
| 13 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | a medication record keeps `substanceAdministration/id` as `identifier` (`mapIdentifiers`, as every other statement). Test `test/medication-activity.test.ts` | the id was used only as the resource id when it was a bare UUID, so an Epic medication (OID root + extension) had no identifier: GA keyed it by content hash and could not match it to the record it already holds | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/13-medication-identifiers.md` |
| 14 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | a Medication Activity in the Medications section (any of its 4 roots) becomes a `MedicationStatement` whatever its mood (EVN or INT): status from statusCode (`MEDICATION_STATEMENT_STATUSES`: active, completed, aborted → stopped, suspended → on-hold, nullified → entered-in-error, else unknown), `effectivePeriod` (or `effectiveDateTime`), `dateAsserted` from the author time, `dosage`. Plan of Treatment substanceAdministrations stay `MedicationRequest` with row 12's intent. Upstream tests that read a Medications entry as MedicationRequest (`medication-dose`, `nullflavor`, `narrative-reference`, `section-template-order`, `synthetic-fixture`, and row 12's fork test `keeps intent order for a Medication Activity in INT mood`) read the statement. Test `test/medication-activity.test.ts` | "taking" was downgraded to "ordered" (the Microsoft path makes MedicationStatement from every Medications entry, EVN or INT; owner ruling: a medication list entry is what the patient takes); GA's medication list and currency rule read the record kind. Upstream may prefer the IG's mood → intent route (CF-MedActivityMood: EVN → plan, INT → order, both MedicationRequest); if it declines, this row stays a GA patch | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/14-medication-statement.md` |
| 15 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `types.ts`, `xml.ts` | a Medication Activity's `entryRelationship/supply`: a Medication Supply Order (`22.4.17`, INT; any mood but EVN) becomes a `MedicationRequest` (intent order, or inside a Plan of Treatment medication that medication's intent (row 12), own id, status, authoredOn and requester from the author, `dispenseRequest` validityPeriod, quantity, `numberOfRepeatsAllowed` = repeatNumber − 1), a Medication Dispense (`22.4.18`, EVN) a `MedicationDispense` (status, quantity, whenHandedOver; `performer`: the author as a performer with function `medicationdispense-performer-function|dataenterer` (who entered it: R4 has no recorder; never a requester or the dispenser), and each C-CDA performer (the dispensing party) as its own performer with no function); medication = the supply's product, else the activity's drug. `processSubstanceAdministration` may return several resources; `CcdaSupply` type; `entryRelationship.supply`, `product.manufacturedProduct`, `supply.performer` parsed as arrays. Test `test/medication-activity.test.ts` | supply orders were silently dropped: the spike's 5 Microsoft-only MedicationRequests on the owner's documents are exactly these (the Microsoft path makes a MedicationRequest from every supply, INT or EVN). Not converted: a supply order's instructions. Identity: a supply with its own id is keyed by it; a planned (INT) medication and its supply order that share one id are both MedicationRequests with the same `identifier[0]`, which GA's engine splits by content hash (its in-batch collision rule, `src/engine.ts`): stable across re-import of the same content; a changed order, or a later document carrying only one of the two, gets a new key and the old record stays (test `a planned medication and its supply order sharing one id are both stored`) | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/15-medication-supplies.md` |

Test `test/observation-value.test.ts` (ported to vitest) | unitless results (INR, pH, specific gravity, ratios) arrived with a name and a date but no result: the spike's 14 dropped REAL values; GA's accounting named them in `notImported` | existing PR medplum#11241 (fixes #11201); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/16-real-values.md` |
| 17 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts` | external PR medplum#11244 applied unchanged (head f6b042b9): `mapObservationEffectiveTime` sets a result observation's and an organizer's `effective[x]` from `@value`, or from an interval: `low` only or `low` = `high` → `effectiveDateTime`, `low` ≠ `high` → `effectivePeriod`, `high` only → `effectivePeriod.end`; a nullFlavor gives nothing. Test `test/observation-effective-time.test.ts` (ported to vitest) | only `effectiveTime/@value` was read: every Epic panel (`<low>`/`<high>`) and many social history observations (`<low>` only) had no date, so GA could not place or match them (the spike's 43 dateless lab panels; its 17 social-history and 3 lab results "only Microsoft" were matched on the same day, so these dateless records are the likely cause) | existing PR medplum#11244 (fixes #11203); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/17-interval-effective-time.md` |

Test `test/observation-interpretation.test.ts` | interpretation (High, Low, Abnormal) was never read: the spike's 30 lab results with an interpretation lost it; the Microsoft path keeps it in that system. GA's `lab_results` shows it and flags out-of-range results by it | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/18-observation-interpretation.md` |
| 19 | `ccda-to-fhir.ts`, `types.ts` | external PR medplum#11243 (head 6af85aab) applied by hand onto rows 1 and 4: an organizer is routed by its own templateIds (`getTemplateIds`); a Family History Organizer (`22.4.45`) becomes one `FamilyMemberHistory` of the patient: relationship (`relatedSubject/code`; none: data-absent `unknown`), sex (`administrativeGenderCode`, FHIR AdministrativeGender), one `condition` per Family History Observation (`22.4.46`) coded by its value, `onsetAge` from its Age Observation (`22.4.31`), `contributedToDeath` from a Death Observation (`22.4.47`); a negated observation gives no condition. `CcdaOrganizer.subject` typed. **GA deviation:** an organizer of any other template stays a panel Observation (the PR keeps only Vital Signs, Result and Functional Status organizers and skips or throws on the rest, which would drop e.g. a Cognitive Status organizer's results). Test `test/family-history.test.ts` (ported to vitest; the PR's "skips an unknown organizer" case replaced by "keeps an organizer of another template") | a relative's disease and age at onset became the patient's own Observations, and the relationship was lost; the Microsoft path makes a FamilyMemberHistory. GA's accounting names a negated or uncoded family history observation and any related observation other than age or death | existing PR medplum#11243 (fixes #11200); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/19-family-history.md` |

Test `test/observation-category.test.ts` | an Epic observation with only a vendor template got `category: []` (invalid FHIR; GA's `lab_results` and `vitals` find records by category), an assessment in Social History lost its social-history class, a Reason for Visit observation had none; the Microsoft path classes every Social History observation `social-history` | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/21-observation-category.md` |

Test `test/observation-coded-ordinal.test.ts` | CDA's CO is a code with an order (dipstick Negative, 1+); the comment called it "Count of individuals", so the code was lost and an empty quantity (UCUM system only) written; the Microsoft path keeps the code. Test `test/planned-observation.test.ts` ("a goal ... stays a Goal, with no empty target or category") | empty objects and arrays are not valid FHIR JSON (a store may refuse the record, a loss); an empty target also reads as a target that is not there | new issue (none open); draft `docs/superpowers/upstream/ccda/24-goal-empty-target.md` |

Upstream already used `import type` for type-only imports; no other syntax needed rewriting.

## Section → resource (with rows 1-24)

Every section's narrative is also on the Composition (`section.text`). Anything a section holds that no row turns into a record is named in GA's `notImported` (src/ccda.ts).

| Section (templateId root) | Entries become | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Problems (22.2.5, .5.1, V2), Health Concerns (22.2.58) | Condition | concern act: one per SUBJ observation (row 9) |
| Allergies (22.2.6, .6.1, V2) | AllergyIntolerance | concern act: one per SUBJ observation (row 9) |
| Medications (22.2.1, .1.1, V2) | MedicationStatement (any mood), keyed by the substanceAdministration id; per supply inside: MedicationRequest (supply order) or MedicationDispense (dispense) | entries-optional root routed (row 1); rows 13-15 |
| Immunizations (22.2.2, .2.1) | Immunization | |
| Family History (22.2.15) | FamilyMemberHistory per Family History Organizer, one condition per observation | row 19 |
| Results, Vital Signs, Social History, Functional Status (22.2.14), Reason for Visit (22.2.12), any other observation section | Observation; a Result Organizer: DiagnosticReport with `result` → its Observations; any other organizer: panel Observation with `hasMember` | the library's "vitals" path; rows 16-18, 20-22 (category: own template, then section; else the section code) |
| Encounters (22.2.22, .22.1) | Encounter; Condition per RSON observation; Condition (`encounter-diagnosis`, `encounter` → its Encounter) per problem observation of an Encounter Diagnosis act (22.4.80) | row 10 |
| Procedures (22.2.7.1) | Procedure | |
| Plan of Treatment (22.2.10) | CarePlan (acts, with their narrative text as `description`), ServiceRequest (observations in a planned mood: INT, PRP, RQO, ARQ), Goal (goal observations), MedicationRequest (substanceAdministrations; `intent` from moodCode); section narrative on the Composition | rows 8, 12, 23 |
| Goals (22.2.60) | Goal | |
| Care Teams (22.2.500) | CareTeam, one participant per member performer (row 4) | |
| Instructions (22.2.45, V2) | DocumentReference (text/plain) | row 5 |
| History of Present Illness (IHE 1.3.6.1.4.1.19376.1.5.3.1.3.4) | DocumentReference (text/plain) | row 5 |
| Notes (22.2.65), e.g. Progress Notes; a Note Activity (22.4.202) in any section | DocumentReference (text/plain) | row 5 |
| Reason for Referral (IHE 1.3.6.1.4.1.19376.1.5.3.1.3.1, V2) | ServiceRequest | row 6 |
| Payers (22.2.18, V2) | Coverage, one per Policy Activity; never shared | row 7 |
| Narrative-only sections (no entries), and entries no row handles | Composition `section.text` | entries named in `notImported` |

## Omitted

- `src/fhir-to-ccda/` (GA only converts C-CDA to FHIR).
- Tests dropped: `roundtrip` and `g9` (both call `convertFhirToCcda`), `b1` (needs upstream `testdata/` sample set of 6 large government files).
- `test/` ported to vitest: explicit `import ... from 'vitest'`, `.ts` imports, `import.meta.dirname` for `__dirname`. `test/synthetic-fixture.test.ts` is GA's own. `testdata/` keeps only the 4 files `nullflavor` reads.

## Build config

- `tsconfig.json` includes `vendor`; it type-checks under GA's strict settings unchanged. `@medplum/core` stays 5.2.14 (no 5.2.15 export needed).
